images.alt: Paulus buigt zijn knieën — Efeziërs 3:14; tekstillustratie.
images.prompt: Use case: historical-scene. Photorealistic illustration of an explicit biblical comparison or event, first-century Roman Judea and Galilee, landscape 3:2, natural materials and daylight, anatomically coherent people with exactly two arms and animals with correct limbs; fully covering modest opaque robes. No modern objects, readable writing, portrait of God the Father, blood, injury or watermark. Ephesians 3:1 and 14–19: Paul calls himself a prisoner and says he bows his knees before the Father to pray for the believers’ inner strength and knowledge of Christ’s love. One adult Paul kneels alone in a modest plain first-century room, wearing fully covering opaque robes, hands naturally clasped in quiet prayer. A simple table with a papyrus roll to one side. Two arms only, natural bent knees and feet under the robe, no God portrait, human divine figure or supernatural visible heart. This illustrates the named prayer posture, not an anonymous large group meeting.

images.alt: Tychikus gaat met het bericht — Efeziërs 6:22; tekstillustratie.
images.prompt: Use case: historical-scene. Photorealistic illustration of an explicit biblical comparison or event, first-century Roman Judea and Galilee, landscape 3:2, natural materials and daylight, anatomically coherent people with exactly two arms and animals with correct limbs; fully covering modest opaque robes. No modern objects, readable writing, portrait of God the Father, blood, injury or watermark. Ephesians 6:21–22 says Paul sends Tychicus to tell the believers how he is and encourage their hearts. Two adult men in a plain first-century room: Paul, described in verse 20 as an ambassador in chains, speaks warmly to Tychicus who is ready to travel with a small shoulder bag. A light simple wrist chain on Paul, no modern prison bars, violence or injury. Exactly two adults with clearly distinct hands. No readable letter text or invented location sign. The focus is entrusting personal news and encouragement, not escape from custody.
